courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: World Regional Geography
courses.description: The study of major world political and natural regions. Course study includes location of the regions on earth, the physical and cultural elements that lend the regions their identities, and ways in which these elements relate to the regions' inhabitants and economies. CSU/UC

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Introduction to the Natural Environment
courses.description: Introduction to the physical elements of geography: maps, earth/sun relationships, meteorology and climatology, natural vegetation, soils, and geomorphology. CSU/UC

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Introduction to the Natural Environment Laboratory
courses.description: Laboratory exercises and experiments designed to explore and understand the primary areas of physical geography. Exercises and applications related to map scales and projections, stereoscopic, topographic and aerial photo interpretation, meteorological tools and models and weather prognostication, geomorphologic models and processes, and landform interpretation. CSU/UC

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Cultural Geography
courses.description: An introductory survey of the geography of culture, and the influences of the physical environment on culture, along with the impact of human activity on the environment, and the role of culture within societies and social groups. The course includes global patterns of population, migration, religion, language, agriculture, politics, customs, resources, and urban and rural settlement. CSU/UC

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Introduction to Weather and Climate
courses.description: This course examines weather and climate patterns of the earth from a geographic perspective including atmospheric structure and composition, solar radiation and energy balances, temperature, seasonal changes, atmospheric moisture, clouds and fog, precipitation, air pressure, winds, air masses and fronts, cyclonic and anticyclonic systems, weather forecasting, adiabatics, climate, and climate change. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: California Geography
courses.description: A thematic approach to the state's issues, processes and topics relevant to the geography including climate, landforms, natural vegetation, water resources, cultural landscape, ethnic diversity, urban and agricultural regions, and the economy. This course explores the physical, and human landscapes that have evolved as a result of the human-environment interface. CSU/UC

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Introduction to Geographic Information Systems
courses.description: This course introduces basic scientific principles of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) as they relate to working with data that have important spatial orientation and organization. Geometric and geographic concepts and theories are used to develop scientific methods for proper communication of the data and the solution of problems that have spatial relationships. Course covers basic concepts in mapping and orientation, the development of map scales and comparison of different coordinate systems and data error analysis. CSU/UC

notes: CU0002 is parsed explicitly; unrecognized catalog layouts are not guessed.
Crosswalk ownership is college-aware; ambiguous ownership remains flagged instead of silently assigned.
CU0321 last-offered data is a planning signal only and does not determine curriculum currency.
DO NOT SCHEDULE rooms are owner-only when a matching owner division is present; they are not campuswide rooms.
Shared portal writes are revalidated server-side; browser-calculated totals are not trusted.
Local database mode writes proposals to SQLite with revision history and stores per-department draft workspaces; static HTML is preview-only for database actions.
Department draft workspaces are isolated by term/college/division/department so switching scope does not destroy unfinished work.
2026-27 credit default is Standardized Attendance Accounting; open-entry/open-exit credit remains Actual Hours / Positive Attendance.
Faculty load caps/factors are configurable planning values, not a contractual certification.
Pathway membership comes only from a confirmed administrator-provided mapping; it is never inferred from course title, TOP code, or division.
Imported existing bookings are a snapshot at generation time, not a live Ad Astra/Colleague connection; regenerate after refreshing the booking export.
Empty optional booking/pathway CSV files are ignored with import warnings; malformed or headerless files produce a clear validation error instead of a raw csv traceback.
RG0547 prepopulation maps prior dates by relative term week + weekday; previous CRNs are retained only as a reference and are never reused as current-term identifiers.
Block schedule alignment is advisory. The planner suggests approved windows and permits documented exceptions rather than blocking CTE/long-format schedules.
Department-chair modality labels are translated to scheduler/Colleague codes from the imported DE coding reference when available.
